A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same RLPO research. Their text, equations, tables, figures, and complete appendices support reliable comparison, including matching material moved between the main text and appendices.

before.justification: v2 reports original concept-generation experiments, search and feedback ablations, human-survey results, fine-tuning analysis, and sentiment-analysis examples.

after.justification: v3 retains original empirical results and adds concept-consistency measurements, classifier-stability comparisons, an engineer usability study, and a CelebA bias experiment.

M1.justification: The DQN seed-selection procedure, VQA preprocessing, TCAV feedback, adaptive rewards, and LoRA preference optimization of Stable Diffusion remain unchanged in Algorithms 1–2 and the corresponding equations. Logistic-regression TCAV scoring was already specified in v2; its new comparison with SGD does not introduce a method component.

E1.justification: Alongside retained ImageNet and IMDB evaluations, v3 adds CelebA blonde-versus-not-blonde classification with gender-bias diagnosis and a distinct task assessing explanations' usefulness to ML engineers. It also introduces concept-targeted synthetic Tiger training images and removes Rabbit examples from the qualitative comparison in Figure 4.

E2.justification: The principal EAC, CRAFT, Lens, greedy-search, human/AI-feedback, LIME, and GradCam comparisons remain. V3 additionally evaluates brute-force preference optimization over every seed prompt without RL (Appendix C.5) and reports an SGD-versus-logistic TCAV comparison (Table 7), which v2 discussed without a corresponding results table.

E3.justification: V3 adds inter-/intra-concept embedding comparisons using Wasserstein distance and Hotelling's T-squared, an equal-time RL/brute-force control, and a two-stage usability study with 19 engineers. Fine-tuning changes from final-layer ResNet50 on ImageNet to GoogleNet using 100 synthetic Tiger images. The ANC metric definition changes despite unchanged Table 1 values. The appendix's human-feedback count changes from seven to eight, matching the eight already stated in v2's main text; this does not establish new recruitment or rerunning.

E4.justification: New analyses test between-concept distinctness and within-concept consistency (Tables 5–6), TCAV classifier stability (Table 7), and optimization with versus without RL under the same time budget (Appendix C.5). Engineer usability, CelebA bias diagnosis, and the revised concept-guided fine-tuning intervention substantially extend the diagnostic evidence. Earlier abstraction, gibberish-prompt, heatmap, and deletion analyses are retained.

E5.justification: V3 introduces explicitly three-trial concept comparisons with uncertainty values, Hotelling's T-squared statistics, and same-distribution judgments in Tables 5–6. Table 7 explicitly reports means and standard deviations across five randomly seeded runs. V2 already contained uncertainty values in other tables, but lacked these documented statistical analyses; the additions do not establish increased runs for retained results. Distribution-test thresholds and p-values are not supplied.

E6.justification: New results include inter-concept cosine similarities of 0.67–0.73 versus 0.99 within concepts, engineer agreement rates of 94.7% and 84.2%, and CelebA TCAV scores of 1.000 for female-face concepts versus 0.000 for male-face concepts. GoogleNet/Tiger fine-tuning replaces the ResNet50/Blue Jay example under different conditions. The Tiger visualization also changes images, concepts, and scores, while Figure 4 loses Rabbit examples. Original search, feedback, recognition-survey, and baseline-comparison table values remain unchanged.

T1.justification: The ANC definition changes from averaging total-normalized frequencies, which collapses to 1/n, to normalizing mean frequency by the maximum frequency (v2 Appendix B.1; v3 Appendix A.1). Property 2 additionally states that TCAV scores are always one beyond t_eta. The three theorems and their remaining derivations are otherwise retained.

C1.justification: Generating model-relevant concepts and generalizing to sentiment analysis remain central claims. V3 explicitly adds bias diagnosis and foregrounds understanding internal representations and engineer usefulness. It drops v2's explicit first-in-concept-based-XAI priority claim for multiple abstraction levels, while retaining that capability in Appendix C.4.

C2.justification: V3 adds interpretations concerning concept consistency, engineer insights, reduced background reliance after fine-tuning, and gender reliance in CelebA classification. Section 5 newly discusses dependence on initial seeds and the generator's capacity and pretraining biases, but removes v2's explicit limitation against real-time use. Domain-mismatch concerns and the inability to select an abstraction level automatically remain.

D1.justification: V3 adds a repository URL and video pointers, documents the 100-image fine-tuning dataset, identifies Stable Diffusion 2 as its source in Figure 29, and supplies usability-survey materials and an IRB identifier. The old ResNet50 checkpoint and final-layer SGD recipe are removed with the replaced experiment, without an equivalent new optimizer recipe. Core DQN, LoRA, preprocessing, and hardware details remain.

R1.justification: V3 adds references supporting newer diffusion models, RL applications, CelebA, bias diagnosis, and LIME, while removing the He et al. ResNet reference. Positioning against concept-retrieval methods remains substantially unchanged. The VLM-related-work passage moves into Section 2; publication updates for existing references do not constitute new cited works.

P1.justification: V3 revises the title, edits the abstract and introductory framing, rewrites the limitations discussion, and reorganizes application subsections. VLM related work moves into the main text, while abstraction and LIME/GradCam discussions move into dedicated appendix subsections. Most methodological explanations and proof text remain closely matched.

P2.justification: The main paper changes to a two-column conference layout, and the opening conceptual diagrams are redrawn and reordered. V3 adds three analysis tables and figures for bias, RL/brute-force comparison, synthetic training data, and usability materials, while replacing the fine-tuning and Tiger displays. Abstraction and LIME/GradCam figures move to the appendix, and Figure 4 is reduced by removing its Rabbit row.

improvement.justification: V3 strengthens evidence for consistency and practical usefulness through Tables 5–7, the concept-guided fine-tuning intervention, and the engineer usability study. Correcting ANC and acknowledging seed and generator biases also improve clarity. These gains are limited by the narrow consistency/usability evaluations, unspecified distribution-test thresholds, and missing optimizer details for the replacement fine-tuning experiment. Removing the explicit real-time limitation is another small loss, but the net effect is positive.
